key_insight: ExplAIner is a declarative query language that unifies many explanation types for classification models while keeping evaluation complexity tightly characterized.
engineering_relevance: It gives practitioners a SAT-solver-friendly way to specify and compute diverse explanations with predictable complexity bounds for Boolean model classes.
method: Extends FOIL with richer vocabulary and layered query structure.
Expresses abductive, contrastive, feature-based, and distance-based explanations.
Adds Opt-FOIL to support minimal explanations under strict partial orders.
evidence_signal: The paper proves formal complexity results: ExplAIner queries fall in the Boolean hierarchy under tractability assumptions, and Opt-FOIL evaluation is in FP^NP, implying fixed SAT-solver call bounds.
watch_item: The guarantees rely on model classes where basic predicates are polynomial-time evaluable, so scalability and applicability depend on the underlying representation.
paper_title: ExplAIner: A Declarative Query Language for Explaining Classification Models
